Create one fresh image entirely from text, no reference images. Square 1024x1024 final artwork.
Use case: stylized-concept.
Style is the absolute priority: authentic early-1990s LucasArts VGA point-and-click adventure background and sprite art, specifically the hand-painted 256-color pixel art language of Monkey Island 2. This must look like actual low-resolution game artwork, not a photograph, not modern smooth digital illustration with a pixel filter. Coarse 320x200-era pixel clusters, economical indexed colors, deliberate checkerboard dithering in gradients, hard pixel edges, painterly environmental shapes translated into low-resolution pixels. Adapt the scene to a square full-bleed canvas without UI.
Composition: a wide establishing view deep inside a moody Caribbean wooden tavern at night, environment dominates; the woman is a SMALL full-body adventure-game sprite, about one-sixth of the canvas height, perched on a stool at a small table, enjoying her lifted coffee cup. A recognizable crescent croissant rests on a plate nearby. Big irregular timber beams, barrels, dim amber lantern pools and cool indigo shadows, an opening onto moonlit tropical water. Layered scenic depth and slightly exaggerated crooked architecture characteristic of this adventure era.
Character: woman in her early 30s, curly auburn shoulder-length hair, freckles, round tortoiseshell glasses, mustard-yellow knit sweater. Express these traits with economical colored pixels at sprite scale; do not enlarge the character to show detail.
No text, captions, letters, logos, signatures, watermarks, UI, dialogue boxes, cursor, borders or panels. Let the period game style fully dictate anatomy, lighting and proportions.

Style is the absolute priority: a convincing frame of rotoscoped animation in the visual language of A Scanner Darkly and Waking Life. The drawing must feel painstakingly traced over live-action footage: natural adult anatomy and unglamorous observed gesture, but every surface rebuilt from flat irregular color islands, unstable slightly doubled hand-traced contour lines, wobbling contours, swimming planes and drifting perspective. Angular painterly blocks within skin, hair, fabric and objects; outlines vary in weight and slightly lose registration. No photorealistic textures, no photographic filter, no smooth 3D render.

The cafe tabletop cuts obliquely across the lower edge with a croissant nearby in the foreground. Behind her, a trippy suburban coffee shop with fluorescent ceiling panels and a large window looking onto a quiet parking lot; wall corners and window geometry subtly bend and drift. Strange lime fluorescent light, dusty mauve, faded teal and warm ochre skin planes, uneasy yet contemplative everyday atmosphere.
Character: woman in her early 30s, curly auburn shoulder-length hair in irregular traced masses, freckles visible in profile, round tortoiseshell glasses, mustard-yellow knit sweater represented by moving flat color shapes.
The rotoscope medium dictates the whole picture, including background. No text, captions, letters, signatures, logos or watermarks.
